title: The distinguished return sheet is a clopen immersion
statement: For finite fields k₁/k₀, locally finite-type schemes X/k₀ and C/k₁, an open immersion c:C→X, and v:Cbar→Xbar with v;pr_X=pr_C;c and v;b_X=b_C;Spec(τ⁻¹), where τ:k₁bar≃ₖ₀k₀bar is the fixed closure isomorphism and b denotes closure projection, v is an open immersion. If c is also a closed immersion, v is a closed immersion. Neither geometric connectedness nor the return power nor smoothness is needed.

source.place: Paragraphs 1--3 and 7: geometric constituents, two-point curve restriction and local Frobenius powers; geometric socle/Frobenius orbit step in sk-i-dl-general-real.

proof.text: An algebraic closure of a finite field is a directed union of finite etale field extensions. Therefore its geometric fibre projections are weakly etale. Cancel the target projection to make v weakly etale. The two projection equations make v monic. Finite type over a locally Noetherian target gives finite presentation, so flat monomorphism implies open immersion.

proof.text: The geometric-fibre projections are integral. Cancel the separated target projection from the integral composite to make v integral and hence closed. Its closed range and open immersion imply closed immersion.
